# Decisions

Append-only. Each entry: date, the decision, why, and what would reopen it. Read this when
a rule seems odd; change a rule by adding a new entry, never by editing an old one.

## 2026-09-23 · D1 · Name: Stratum
The project is **Stratum** (layers you dig through). "Residue" survives as the core idea
(what is left after the mundane explanations) and names Phase 2. *Reopen if* the name
collides with an established archaeology project.

## 2026-09-23 · D2 · A static site generated by standard-library Python
The site is built by `scripts/build.py` from the JSON records: no framework, no npm, no
chart library, no database server. Charts are hand-built SVG generated at build time.
*Why:* the owner is not a programmer; zero dependencies means nothing to install and nothing
to rot; every chart redraws itself when records change. *Reopen if* interactivity needs
exceed what small vanilla JS can do (e.g. a real map with zoom).

## 2026-09-23 · D3 · Dense, beautiful, concise design
The owner's standing preference: beautiful but information-dense — tables and bullets, smaller
type, no flourishy narrative or oversized headings. Aletheia's palette lineage (warm paper,
ink, one ochre accent) with a new system: Newsreader for titles, IBM Plex Sans for reading,
Plex Mono for numbers and labels; fate colors always paired with a shape. See
`docs/DESIGN.md`. *Reopen only* at the owner's request.

## 2026-09-23 · D4 · Hard length budgets on every record field
The schema caps each text field (claim 300 chars, objection 220, …) and the build fails on
any overrun. *Why:* keeps the site concise forever, whoever writes the records.

## 2026-09-23 · D5 · Hypotheses pre-registered before any data
H1–H6 were written in `findings/log.md` and pushed to GitHub (commit `0d43f27`) before the
first record existed. They are tested exactly as worded with fixed thresholds. New ideas
become new dated hypotheses; old ones are never reworded.

## 2026-09-23 · D6 · Evidence coded "as it stood at the claim"
`features_at_claim` records the situation within about five years of the claim, with a source
for each value, to limit hindsight bias. Because researchers still know the outcome, a blind
re-coding test is planned (M1 in the findings log).

## 2026-09-23 · D7 · Four agent roles with fixed capabilities
Researcher, skeptic, analyst and scout are defined in `.claude/agents/` with their own model,
effort and tools. The analyst has no web access, so findings can only rest on the checked
catalog. The skeptic is never downgraded to a cheaper model: it is the quality gate.

## 2026-09-23 · D8 · Token discipline after the wave-1 overspend
Wave-1 researchers (Opus) used about 280–320k tokens and 70–105 tool calls per record,
mostly by piping raw Crossref JSON and whole pages or PDFs into context — where every later
step re-reads it. Fixes: `scripts/lookup.py` (citation, abstract and open-access status in a
few lines; `page --grep` for passages), budgets (~40 calls for researchers, ~35 for
skeptics), no private helper scripts. Wave 2 tests Sonnet researchers under Opus skeptics;
the cheapest configuration whose skeptic issue rate stays low wins.

## 2026-09-23 · D9 · Drafts are published, labelled; only reviewed records count
The site shows every valid record so the lab's progress is visible, but unreviewed records
carry a "Draft" label and are excluded from the analysis until a skeptic has passed them
(or the researcher has revised them).

## 2026-09-23 · D10 · Phase 1 to ~60 balanced cases, then Phase 2 alongside it
Phase 1 (anomaly fates) is the teacher: it learns what distinguishes real anomalies from
false ones and ranks today's open cases. Its ceiling is that it can only rank anomalies
someone already noticed. Phase 2 (radiocarbon residue) is the search engine that can surface
anomalies nobody has flagged. Plan: grow Phase 1 to about 60 balanced cases — enough to test
H1–H6 at their thresholds — then run Phase 2 in parallel, using Phase 1's lessons as its
filter. Cost principle for both: **scripts sift the haystack, models judge the needles.**

## 2026-09-23 · D11 · Status reflects the 2026 literature, not popular accounts
Researchers may and should overrule the starter list. First results: White Sands and Bluefish
Caves are recorded as *open* (critiques continue in 2024–26), and Monte Verde — the classic
vindication — was re-contested in 2026 (Surovell et al., *Science*; rebuttal by Waters et al.,
*PaleoAmerica*). Records carry dated timelines so a status can change without rewriting
history.

## 2026-09-23 · D12 · No personal data in API calls
The first version of `check_sources.py` put the owner's email in its User-Agent (a courtesy
convention for scholarly APIs), and one agent reused it in a few OpenAlex queries. Removed;
`scripts/net.py` now identifies the project by its repository URL only. The string remains in
the first commit's history; the same address is already public as the git author email.
